name: European Open Rivers Programme
summary: Grants to prepare for and carry out removal of small dams and weirs across Greater Europe, including barrier identification, pre-demolition work and demolition. No matching funds are required, except that public entities leading a dam removal grant must cover at least 50% of project costs.

parts.RU: as far east as the Urals

amount.note: Cap applies to barrier identification and prioritisation grants only; most other grants have no maximum

steps: Contact relevant authorities and water agencies before applying

eligibility.rule: Public-sector lead applicants can apply only for A3 or Category B.
Public-sector applicants must manage water resources and have river restoration or dam removal experience.
Public-sector leads must have grant staff with river restoration or dam removal expertise.
Public-sector applicants must show commitment to partnering with NGOs and stakeholders.
A repeat A1 applicant needs a follow-on A2 or A4 award for its previous A1 project.
A3 or A4 projects have no known issues that could stop the river staying free-flowing after removal.
Small dam removal takes out the full height of the barrier.

documents: Accounts for the past three financial years
Lead partner’s statutes as proof of legal status
Evidence of relevant work by supporting partners, if involved
River system diagram showing distances (A2, A3, A4 and B)
Catchment map showing the barriers (A2, A3, A4 and B)
At least three photos showing the barrier, upstream impoundment and downstream river (A2, A3, A4 and B)
Available engineering or technical design documents (A2, A3, A4 and B)

effort.quote: We are currently not accepting applications. The next call for applications will be open from 1st February until 5th March 2027.
Your application will be reviewed by the Programme’s management team and our independent grant selection panel.
We require that applicants contact relevant authorities, municipalities, and water agencies early in the process (before applying to a grant).

eligibility.quote: Public entities applying as lead project partners are only eligible to apply for an A3 dam removal grant or a Category B grant.
To apply for a grant as a publicly funded entity, you must manage water resources and have proven experience in river restoration and/or dam removal.
It is essential that the staff managing the grant have relevant expertise in these areas; general agency experience alone will not suffice.
Applicants must also show a commitment to forming partnerships with NGOs and other stakeholders for the project’s implementation.
We will not support more than one A1 (identification project) unless your previous project/s have been awarded a follow-on dam removal (A2 pre-demolition, or A4 dam removal grant).
The programme supports the removal of man-made barriers such as dams, weirs, culverts, sills, sluices or fords. We do not support the removal of natural barriers.
We will require you to confirm that no known issues might jeopardise the river from remaining free flowing once the dam(s) have been removed.
We require that all small dam removal projects remove the entire vertical extent of the dam (i.e. the full height).

co_finance.quote: A public entity applying as the lead partner must provide at least 50% of the project costs, as the programme will only contribute up to 50%.

after_award.quote: A grant is usually disbursed in three portions: the first part upon contract signature, the second following approval of an interim progress report, and the last following approval of a final report and successful completion of the project.

documents.quote: All applicants must send us accounts for the past three financial years.
As a part of the application process, we ask that applicants provide a budget and schedule of activities.
Copies of statutes to show legal status
Required: Please upload a diagram of the river system showing the above distances.
Upload a map of the catchment (mandatory) indicating the barriers.
Upload at least three photos and optional video (facing the barrier, the upstream impoundment and the river directly downstream of the barrier).
Upload any technical documents such as engineering and/or technical design plans.
